title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): Grothendieck wants to enlarge the 'Galois–Teichmüller' category. Its objects are punctured compact surfaces (or algebraic curves over C). Its morphisms so far are finite étale coverings X→Y. He now wants to add the open inclusions X = Y∖T ↪ Y, i.e. 'bouchage des trous' (filling in punctures). For the enlarged class of morphisms to be closed under composition, he is led to the general morphism shown in diagram (24). In it, X ⊂ X̂ and Y = Ŷ∖T ⊂ Ŷ, and X̂→Ŷ is a finite, possibly ramified map of compact surfaces. Write S = X̂∖X. Then S contains S0 = X̂|T, the preimage of T. The extra punctures S1 = S∖S0 lie over genuine (unpunctured) points of Y, and some of them may be ramification points.

This page, step by step:

(1) Isotopy. In the topological setting, the reasonable notion of isotopy for such f is equivalence under conjugation by Aut°(X)×Aut°(Y). Here Aut°(X) means homeomorphisms of X̂ preserving S (identity component), and Aut°(Y) means homeomorphisms of Ŷ preserving T. So an isotopy class is an orbit (u,v)·f = v∘f∘u⁻¹.

(2) The obstruction. Such f does factor: X ↪ X' := X̂∖S0 (fill the holes S1), followed by X' → Y. Here X'→Y is a finite cover, unramified except over finitely many points B ⊂ Y. Those points are not punctures of Y and are not fixed by the isotopy class.
- This factorization is not canonical at the level of isotopy classes. Aut(Ŷ,T) can move the branch points B inside Y, so the middle object and the 'hole-filling' factor are only determined up to point-pushing.
- In modern terms: the forgetful map Mod(X̂,S) → Mod(X̂,S0) has the point-pushing (Birman) kernel.
- A ramified cover over non-marked points is not an isotopy-invariant datum relative to (Ŷ,T).
Hence the isotopy classes of morphisms of the enlarged category do not decompose canonically into 'inclusion classes' followed by 'covering classes'.

(3) Consequence. Grothendieck says he no longer sees how to interpret 'nos belles classes' as abstract topological objects over C. These are presumably the isotopy classes forming the Hom-sets of the Teichmüller/Galois–Teichmüller category, together with their images in a suitable profinite completion. The algebraic interpretation over C is the one used to let Gal(Q̄/Q) act.

(4) Where it goes next. On the next page he retreats to something weaker: a functor from the Teichmüller groupoid of type (g,ν), with a chosen subset I of ν' punctures, to that of type (g,ν−ν') by filling the holes in I. This is the forgetful map M_{g,ν}→M_{g,ν−ν'} on π1 / fundamental groupoids, with transitivity for successive fillings. He also notes the difficulty of composing these with the covering morphisms of the (non-groupoid) Galois–Teichmüller category.

Purpose: build a category, not just a groupoid, on which Gal(Q̄/Q) acts, combining coverings and point-forgetting. This page records why the naive combination fails.
errors: No mathematical error. Grothendieck's diagnosis is correct: the factorization exists but is not canonical up to isotopy, because branch points over unmarked points of Y are not rigidified by Aut(Ŷ,T). The page is a statement of difficulty, not a claim of proof.
Previous-page transcription has 'T = Ŷ − T', which should be 'T = Ŷ ∖ Y'.

ideas.what: Isotopy of morphisms X→Y of punctured surfaces given by ramified covers X̂→Ŷ plus extra punctures: orbits of Aut(X̂,S)°×Aut(Ŷ,T)° acting by conjugation
ideas.modern_name: Isotopy classes of branched covers relative to marked points; Hurwitz-type equivalence of covers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Hurwitz); modern mapping-class-group treatments (Birman–Hilden, Fried, etc.)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and coverings informally; this precise definition is not recalled

ideas.what: Non-canonicity of factoring such a morphism into a hole-filling inclusion followed by a (ramified) covering, at the level of isotopy classes
ideas.modern_name: Point-pushing / Birman exact sequence kernel; non-functoriality of branched covers under the forgetful map

ideas.what: Goal of a Galois–Teichmüller category (not groupoid) containing both coverings and 'bouchage des trous', with profinite completions of its classes interpreted algebraically over C
ideas.modern_name: Teichmüller tower with point-erasing maps; Galois action compatible with covers and forgetful maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984); developed by Drinfeld (GT, 1990), Ihara, Nakamura, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §2 (Teichmüller tower, 'operations' on the modular groupoids)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly abandons interpreting the classes of a category combining branched coverings and point-filling as topological objects over C. He identifies the obstruction as the lack of canonical factorization. A clean categorical framework for this mixed category, with Galois action, is not standard. Approaches via Hurwitz spaces and moduli of admissible covers address related issues without being framed this way.
missed.quote: L'ennui, c'est qu'il n'y a plus de factorisation canoniques d'une classe d'isotopie ... je ne vois plus comment interpréter nos belles classes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a precisely located obstruction to a 'Galois–Teichmüller category with covers'. It may be useful context for work on GT actions compatible with both covers and forgetful maps (Nakamura, Schneps, Hoshi–Mochizuki-type combinatorial anabelian results). It is unlikely to be new to specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful working-note diagnosis of an expected difficulty (point-pushing and moving branch points) in extending the Teichmüller tower to a category with covers. It is historically illuminating as a record of the path toward the Esquisse's groupoid formulation, but contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: 'le morphisme vers le groupe' is likely 'la conjugaison sous le groupe' (isotopy = conjugation by Aut°(X)×Aut°(Y)).
'(où Aut°(X) est interprété comme Aut(X̂,S), et Aut(Y) comme Aut(Ŷ,T))': the second should be read as Aut°(Y).
'(dans leur ci-dessus(' is unclear; probably '(dans les conditions/cas ci-dessus'.
'en des parties ouvertes de Y' should mathematically be 'en des points de Y' (S1 is a finite set); the reading is uncertain.
'Y' est un morphisme fini' should be read as 'Y'→Y est un revêtement fini, génériquement non ramifié...'.
The phrase about 'points de Y qui ne sont pas distingués' is possibly 'pas déterminés' by the given class.
